situation: Third place, back straight. {rival} is close enough to read your number plate, and you picked up a banana two corners ago.
prompt: What do you do with the banana?

diagram.caption: {rival} on your bumper. The banana is still in your hands.

answers.label: Hold it behind the kart and keep driving
answers.response: This one habit will win you more races than any other. Hold the item button and the banana trails along behind you, so anything arriving at your back bumper — a green shell, a red shell, {rival} herself — hits the banana instead of you. It costs nothing to carry. So carry it.

answers.label: Drop it now so she has to swerve
answers.response: It will make her swerve, and a banana sitting still on a wide straight is easy to see coming. The bigger problem is that the second it leaves your hands your back is bare again — and the back is where the shells arrive from.

answers.label: Throw it forward, up the road
answers.response: Thrown forward, a banana lands ahead of you — which means you are now the one who has to dodge it. Bananas go behind you, or they stay in your hands.

takeaway: Anything held behind the kart is armour, and holding it is free.

situation: A green shell in your hands. {rival} is three or four kart lengths up the road, wandering about between the kerbs.
prompt: What is the green shell for?

diagram.caption: She is ahead, but not exactly holding a straight line.

answers.label: Hold it behind you as armour
answers.response: Green shells fly dead straight and never turn, so landing one on a moving kart is mostly luck even for people who play a lot. Held behind you, the same shell blocks everything that comes at your back, every single time. No aiming, and it works on every lap.

answers.label: Fire it at her
answers.response: She is weaving, the shell goes straight, and most of these end up rattling off a barrier somewhere. You have spent your armour on a maybe — and now the next thing to come up behind you arrives at an empty bumper.

answers.label: Wait for a corner where she cannot dodge
answers.response: By then something will have hit you from behind and you will not have it any more. It is already doing its best work right now, sitting behind you.

takeaway: Green shells are armour first. Aiming is a skill; holding is a habit — and the habit wins more races.

situation: Triple bananas. Three of them, spinning round and round your kart.
prompt: Do you need to hold the item button?

diagram.caption: They circle you on their own.

answers.label: No — they are already protecting you
answers.response: Triples orbit your kart by themselves, and anything that hits one is something that did not hit you. Nothing to hold. Just drive, and when you do spend one, put it somewhere useful.

answers.label: Yes, or they do nothing
answers.response: Holding is for one item at a time. A set of three circles you as it is — the button is only for letting them go, one at a time.

answers.label: Throw them all quickly before you lose them
answers.response: Then you are bare again, having aimed at nobody in particular. Going round and round your kart, they are doing more for you than they ever will lying on the tarmac.

takeaway: Triples guard you by themselves. Hold nothing, drive on, spend them one at a time.

situation: A bob-omb, and it is ticking. {rival} is right behind you.
prompt: What do you do with the bob-omb?

answers.label: Throw it backwards, straight away
answers.response: Backwards is where she is, and the blast is wide enough that you do not have to be accurate about it — which makes this one of the few throws in the game you cannot really miss with. Do it now: a bob-omb goes off on its own eventually, and it does not care whose it was.

answers.label: Hold it behind you like a banana
answers.response: Everything else, yes. Not this one. It is counting down the whole time it is in your hands, and when it goes off back there you are well within range.

answers.label: Throw it forward at the pack ahead
answers.response: It will go off somewhere up the road, which is precisely where you are about to be driving. Bombs go backwards.

takeaway: Hold everything — except the one that is counting down. Bombs go backwards, immediately.

situation: A red shell. {rival} is somewhere up ahead, out of sight round the bend.
prompt: What do you do with the red shell?

diagram.caption: She is round the corner, where you cannot even see her.

answers.label: Fire it forward
answers.response: This is the one item genuinely worth using rather than hoarding. A red shell steers itself: send it off and it goes and finds whoever is ahead of you, round corners, without you aiming at anything at all. Nothing else in the game gives you a hit for so little effort.

answers.label: Hold it behind you as armour
answers.response: It does work back there — a red shell blocks like anything else. But it is the only thing you own that can score a hit without you aiming, so using it as a plain wall wastes what makes it special. Hold a banana; fire the red.

answers.label: Wait until you can actually see her
answers.response: You never need to see her. That is the entire point of a red shell — it does the looking for you, round bends and over hills.

takeaway: Hold everything, fire the red shells. They are the only item that aims for you.

situation: The warning is up: a red shell is locked on to you from behind. There is a banana in your hands.
prompt: What do you do about the red shell?

answers.label: Hold the item button and keep driving your line
answers.response: The banana sits behind your bumper and the shell hits that instead of you. It costs nothing and it works every time — which is why the warning is really a reminder to hold the button, not a puzzle to solve.

answers.label: Swerve left and right to shake it off
answers.response: Red shells steer. Following you is the whole thing they do, so all the swerving achieves is arriving at the next corner sideways — and then it hits you anyway.

answers.label: Drop the banana on the road behind you
answers.response: Now it is lying somewhere back there and the shell is still coming for you. Held, it cannot miss. There is no reason to turn a certainty into a maybe.

takeaway: A red shell warning means hold the button. It is not a dodging puzzle — you cannot outrun something that steers.

situation: Both your item slots are full: a banana, and a coin you have not bothered spending. A row of item boxes is coming up.
prompt: What do you do before you reach the item boxes?

diagram.caption: Two slots, both full, and free items straight ahead.

answers.label: Spend the coin on the way in, so there is room
answers.response: You can carry two things, and if both slots are full you drive straight through the box and get nothing at all. Cashing in the coin on the approach turns a wasted box into a fresh item — and keeps the banana, which is the one actually doing a job.

answers.label: Nothing — driving through will swap one out
answers.response: It will not. A full pair of slots means the box does nothing whatsoever. You will sail through a free item and come out the other side holding exactly what you went in with.

answers.label: Dump both, to be sure of getting something good
answers.response: Then you arrive at the boxes with an empty bumper, which is the one thing worth avoiding. Spend the junk, keep the armour.

takeaway: Two slots, and a full pair means the next box is wasted. Clear the junk on the way in — never the armour.

situation: You are about to spend a banana purely to free up a slot. There is a row of item boxes just ahead.
prompt: Where do you drop the banana?

diagram.caption: Everybody has to drive at the boxes. Nobody has a choice about it.

answers.label: Right on the item boxes
answers.response: Everybody drives at the boxes — they have no choice, that is where the items are. A banana sitting on one is about the closest thing to a free hit in the game, and you did not have to aim at a single person to set it up.

answers.label: Anywhere, it makes no difference
answers.response: It is the same button press either way, so you may as well put it somewhere people are guaranteed to drive. Two seconds of thought, one free spin-out later on.

answers.label: On the widest part of the straight
answers.response: That is the easiest place on the whole track to steer around. Bananas earn their keep where people cannot avoid them: item boxes, ramps, the inside of a tight corner.

takeaway: If you are dumping something, dump it where everyone has to drive. Item boxes and ramps.

situation: First place, and the box hands you… a coin. Again.

diagram.caption: Out in front, which is where the game hands you coins.

answers.label: Yes — use it straight away
answers.response: Coins are not nothing. Each one makes you a little faster, up to ten, and you lose three of them every time something hits you — so you are usually topping back up rather than getting greedy. Spending it also clears the slot, so the next box can hand you something with teeth.

answers.label: No — it is a wasted item, ignore it
answers.response: In first place a coin is about half of what you will ever be given, so ignoring them means ignoring half your item boxes. Two coins and an empty slot beats nothing and a blocked one.

answers.label: Save it in case you need the speed later
answers.response: Coins do not keep. They are a small top-up now, and until you spend it, it is a blocked slot stopping you picking up anything better.

takeaway: In first, half your boxes are coins. Spend them the moment they arrive: a little speed, and room for the next one.

situation: Second lap. You have been sitting on a mushroom since the last item box, and the hairpin is coming up fast.
prompt: When do you use the mushroom?

diagram.caption: The hairpin, and the long straight after it.

answers.label: As the corner opens up onto the straight
answers.response: A mushroom gives you the same burst wherever you use it, so it is worth the most when you are slowest — and you are never slower than on the way out of a corner. Wait for the exit, then go.

answers.label: Halfway round the hairpin, to get through it quicker
answers.response: A boost in the middle of a corner mostly boosts you into the barrier. The kart goes where it is pointing, and halfway round a hairpin it is pointing at the wall.

answers.label: Save it in case {rival} catches up
answers.response: Saving a mushroom for later usually means holding it forever — there is always one more reason to wait. And unlike a banana, it does nothing for you while you carry it.

takeaway: Mushrooms are for the moment you stop being slow: corner exit, then the straight.
